item.title: ReasoningBank: Agent Memory That Learns From Failures
item.description:
ReasoningBank is a memory framework for LLM agents from Google that stores lessons, not logs. After each task, the agent judges whether it succeeded, then writes down a few general reasoning strategies, including warnings from its failures. On new tasks it retrieves the closest lessons. On WebArena with Gemini 2.5 Flash, it lifted success from 40.5% to 48.8%.

The paper is “ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory” by Siru Ouyang, Jun Yan, Chen-Yu Lee, Tomas Pfister and 13 co-authors (arXiv 2509.25140), accepted at ICLR 2026. It also introduces MaTTS, a way to spend extra compute per task to produce better memories.
